title: What do the four sides of this hollow grid add up to?
description: A grid of nine tiles has an empty middle. Each side is added one number at a time, with a plus number moving up and a minus number moving down, and all four sides turn out to give the same total. Keeko's doubt that the top row makes thirteen, because the minus signs were dropped, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the numbers on a side one at a time, treating a minus number as a move down, and all four sides share one total called the border sum. Watch for the slip of dropping the minus signs and adding the digits.

source: Second hollow grid: top row 5, -3, -5; middle row 0, (empty), -5; bottom row -8, -2, 7
video_script.why: The child adds three numbers with signs along each side of a hollow grid and finds that every side gives the same total, the border sum.
video_script.substitution: The book's own second hollow grid. A small example of four, negative one and negative two on a lift shows the one-at-a-time adding first.
video_script.anchor: a square of nine tiles from the book, with the middle tile missing
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the top row makes thirteen, because five and three and five add up to thirteen. He dropped the minus signs, and negative three and negative five move down, so the top row is negative three.
video_script.payoff_line: All four sums are negative three, so the border sum is negative three.

final_answer.spoken: all four sums are negative three, so the border sum is negative three

maths_rules: grid: top row 5, -3, -5; middle row 0, (empty), -5; bottom row -8, -2, 7
add one number at a time: a plus number moves up, a minus number moves down
all four sums are -3, so the border sum is -3
slip: dropping the minus signs gives 5 + 3 + 5 = 13 for the top row

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>To add numbers with signs, think of moving on an upright number line.
A plus number moves us up. A minus number moves us down.
<bookmark mark='demo'/>Start at four. Four plus negative one is three. Three plus negative two is one.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Suppose all four sides of a grid add up to one number.
That number is called the border sum.
